content:
The paramagnetic coupling term (orbital Zeeman energy) for a hydrogen atom in a magnetic field \(B = 1\,\text{T}\) and small orbital magnetic quantum number \(m\) is on the order of \(\mu_B B\), where \(\mu_B = 9.27 \times 10^{-24}\,\text{J/T}\) is the Bohr magneton. This gives an energy of approximately \(9.27 \times 10^{-24}\,\text{J} \approx 5.8 \times 10^{-5}\,\text{eV}\).

The transition energy \(\Delta E\) for a wavelength \(\lambda = 0.4861\,\mu\text{m} = 486.1\,\text{nm}\) (the H-beta line) is \(\Delta E = \frac{hc}{\lambda} \approx 2.55\,\text{eV}\).

Comparing the two: \(5.8 \times 10^{-5}\,\text{eV} \ll 2.55\,\text{eV}\). Therefore, the paramagnetic coupling term is much smaller than the transition energy.

Answer: B
